messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: BrightMart performance & surge-readiness checklist

Hi Olivia — great to meet you and Samir on the call earlier. Quick follow-up capturing the performance discussion and the open questions we agreed to surface. I want to make sure we're aligned on success criteria for the PoC and what we'll validate during the benchmark window.

Key SLO targets you outlined on the call (please correct if I got anything wrong):
- Client-visible p95 latency for streaming generation (avg response length ~400 tokens): <= 200 ms tail for token emission after stream starts (network excluded)
- Sustained concurrency: 200 concurrent streaming sessions
- Sustained throughput: ~10k tokens/sec aggregate across sessions
- Burst capacity: absorb spikes up to 800 concurrent sessions for up to 10 minutes with graceful queueing afterwards
- Scale-up time target: 3 minutes from idle to 80% of burst capacity (warm pool allowed)
- Queueing behavior: FIFO with max wait TTL 90s; if TTL exceeded, fail-open to a smaller model (lower-cost) or return 503 depending on route

Open questions we promised to answer:
1) Warm pool sizing and warmup cost assumptions (Neha will propose numbers).
2) How we surface partial tokens/streaming handshake latency for browser websockets vs. native sockets.
3) Which fallback model we route to during extreme load (quality drop/latency tradeoffs).
4) Cost estimate for the PoC and a sample production run with the above SLOs.

Next steps (proposed):
- Neha: share benchmark plan + expected warm pool config by EOD tomorrow (attached plan).
- Connor: send a mutual action plan with target dates and responsibilities (I will send a draft).
- BrightMart: confirm the test dataset, sample traffic profile, and legal contact for the PoC order.

Attachments: bm_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf (benchmark plan stub), redwood_surge_config.csv (example config)

Thanks — Connor

--

Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightMart performance & surge-readiness checklist

Connor — thanks for the recap, that matches what we said on the call. A few clarifications from our side before Neha's plan lands:

- The p95 target is measured from when our client SDK sees the first token to when the last of the initial response chunk is emitted. Network variability will be captured on our side but we need the server-side emission time to be the <=200ms window.
- For burst behavior: the 800 concurrent sessions is a realistic peak during BFCM traffic for one checkout region. We need the PoC to validate both scale-up time and correctness under backpressure (no message loss).
- Regarding queue TTL: 90s is acceptable but we need to define what the user sees in the UI when queue TTL expires (retry/backoff guidance).

One more ask: can you provide an example of the streaming handshake (CORS + websocket upgrade) latency and whether Redwood supports chunked transfer fallback? We have some clients that cannot use websockets during peak hours.

I'll send our test dataset and a short traffic profile doc by Monday. Also copying Samir for infra-level constraints.

— Olivia
VP Engineering, BrightMart Commerce

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@brightmart.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightMart performance & surge-readiness checklist — benchmark plan + numbers attached

Hi Olivia — attaching the benchmark plan (bm_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf) and a suggested surge config (redwood_surge_config.csv). Summary answers to your asks below.

Warm pool and scale-up assumptions (example PoC config):
- Warm pool: 40 prewarmed instances (model shard count optimized for your model family), each capable of ~20 concurrent streaming sessions at p95 <=200ms for 400-token outputs (gives ~800 concurrent headroom).
- Cold-start path: adding new instances uses fast image layering; first usable throughput typically available in ~90s but hot-throughput (kernel/JIT primed) reaches target in ~3 minutes.
- Cost note: warm pool carries baseline cost equal to X GPU-hours/day — we'll convert to $/day in the formal estimate.

Queueing and fallback policy:
- Default: FIFO queue, per-session TTL 90s.
- If TTL expires: route to a lightweight 7B quantized model (approx 30% higher latency for same token size but 60% lower cost) OR return a structured retry suggestion. We will expose the fallback decision in the response header so your client can adjust UX.

Streaming handshake / non-websocket fallback:
- Websocket handshake median added latency: 8–12 ms (our infra at edge) — token emission latency measured post-handshake.
- Chunked HTTP (server-sent events / chunked transfer) supported as fallback; token emit characteristics are the same once the connection is established but the handshake path differs and can add 20–40 ms depending on proxying. We recommend testing both paths; plan includes both websocket and SSE scenarios.

Benchmark plan highlights (see attached):
- Two phases: warm-up (3 hours with ramping traffic) + validation (3 x 30 minute sustained runs at target concurrency + 3 x burst tests of 10 minutes to 800 concurrent).
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 token emission latency, connection handshake time, queue wait distribution, success/fallback rate, per-route cost.

I'll stand by to run these with you on a mutually scheduled window. Connor — I've put tentative PoC dates in the MAP below.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Thanks Neha — couple of infra constraints from our side:
- We terminate TLS at our edge (Fastly) which does some connection pooling. We will provide a staging edge config but need guidance on keep-alive/connection lifetime recommendations for long-lived streaming sessions.
- Some of our older clients retry aggressively; can Redwood surface a per-session idempotency token so our clients can dedupe on reconnects?
- For compliance: we need to confirm that the PoC does not persist user PII in logs by default; if logs are necessary, they must be redacted or encrypted.

If you can call out the exact headers you will add to responses (e.g., x-redwood-fallback, x-redwood-queued-ttl) that will speed integration.

Samir
Principal Infra Engineer, BrightMart

- Week of Aug 9: infra prep & shared staging config (Samir owns).
- Aug 16–18: Warm-up and tuning (Neha leading).
- Aug 19–20: Validation runs + burst tests (joint runbook).
- Aug 23: Review results; produce recommendation and costs (Redwood + BrightMart).

Owners / inputs needed:
- BrightMart: staging edge config, test dataset, list of client populations to simulate (Olivia / Samir).
- Redwood: benchmark scripts, warm pool config, response headers, fallback model and quantization profile (Neha / Marissa).
- Legal/Procurement: PO and minimal SOW (Connor).

Deliverables:

- Integration notes (headers, handshake guidance, SSE fallback).
- Proposed production config for 24x7 with recommended warm pool and expected $/hour.

Action items this week:
1) BrightMart to confirm PoC window and provide staging edge details by Mon Jul 27.
2) Redwood (Neha) to share concrete warm pool cost estimate and updated benchmark plan (final) by Mon Jul 27.
3) Connor to send procurement contact and draft SOW.
